title: Why Your Phone Charges Slower After About 80 Percent
fb_caption: Your phone races to about 80 percent, then crawls the rest of the way, and that's on purpose. At first the charger pushes a strong, steady current. Near full, the battery reaches its voltage limit, so the charger holds it there and lets the current taper off. Many phones also learn your routine, pause around 80 percent overnight, and finish just before you wake up, because sitting at a full charge for hours wears a battery faster. Do you charge your phone overnight, or top it up during the day?
engagement_comment: Do you charge your phone overnight, or top it up during the day? 1 = overnight, every night, 2 = quick top-ups, 3 = whenever it turns red.

beats.text: Your phone races to about eighty percent, then crawls the rest of the way. That's on purpose.
At first, the charger pushes a strong, steady current, and the battery fills up really fast.
Near full, the battery hits its voltage limit, so the charger holds it there and lets the current taper off.
Here's the twist. Some phones learn your routine, hold around eighty percent overnight, and finish just before you wake up.
Sitting at a full charge for hours wears a battery faster, so that pause helps it last longer.
Do you charge your phone overnight, or top it up during the day? Tell us below.
